FROM INSTALLATION TO YOUR FIRST PROJECT

A beginning,
with context.

Try the CSHCLI 0.7.0 local workflow: create a project, save a decision and acquire a file lease. You do not need an AI account for these steps.

Requires Python 3.11+ with pip and two terminals on the same machine for the manual workflow.

Prefer guided setup? After installation, run & $cli start in PowerShell or "$cli" start in Bash. The assistant configures your session and project and starts the coordinator when needed. You can use it without running serve separately. The walkthrough below explains the manual commands.

Watch the website walkthrough

Silent video with Spanish on-screen text. It shows changing the preview, choosing Windows or Linux and opening this guide. The website terminal examples are illustrative; they do not execute the CLI.

1. Prepare2. Coordinator3. Project4. Memory5. LeaseNext step
01 / YOUR OWN ENVIRONMENT

Prepare your workspace.

Open a working folder and run the block for your system. A virtual environment keeps this installation separate from your other projects. The package downloads from the GitHub main branch, which may change.

Windows · PowerShell
py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install "https://github.com/jtpydk5gyh-alt/cshcli/archive/refs/heads/main.zip"
$cli = (Resolve-Path .venv\Scripts\cshcli.exe).Path
& $cli --version
macOS and Linux · Bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install "https://github.com/jtpydk5gyh-alt/cshcli/archive/refs/heads/main.zip"
cli="$PWD/.venv/bin/cshcli"
"$cli" --version

The version prints when installation finishes. If the venv module is missing on Linux, install the package for your distribution. If you use Git in this folder, exclude .venv/ and .cshcli/ before saving files to the repository.

02 / FIRST TERMINAL

Start the coordinator.

Continue in the same terminal. Leave it open while you follow the guide: this process handles requests at http://127.0.0.1:8765 and stores coordination data in .cshcli/coordinator.sqlite3, inside your current folder.

Windows · PowerShell
& $cli serve
macOS and Linux · Bash
"$cli" serve

The coordinator only accepts local connections. If your coordinator already occupies the port, use that process; if another application uses it, consult cshcli serve --help and set the same URL in both terminals with CSHCLI_URL.

03 / SECOND TERMINAL

Your identity. Your project.

Open another terminal in the same working folder. Choose an unregistered local alias and run the block once. The token is captured in a variable without printing it. CSHCLI_TOKEN identifies you to the coordinator; it is separate from your AI provider keys.

Windows · PowerShell
$cli = (Resolve-Path .venv\Scripts\cshcli.exe).Path
$identity = & $cli auth register my-alias | ConvertFrom-Json
$env:CSHCLI_TOKEN = $identity.token
Remove-Variable identity
$project = & $cli project create my-project | ConvertFrom-Json
$projectId = $project.id
& $cli project list
macOS and Linux · Bash
cli="$PWD/.venv/bin/cshcli"
export CSHCLI_TOKEN="$("$cli" auth register my-alias | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])')"
project_id="$("$cli" project create my-project | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')"
"$cli" project list

You should see my-project in the list. Keep your token in a secure manager if you need to reuse this identity: it is only returned during registration, and the pilot does not offer recovery or rotation. The environment variable lasts for this session; do not publish the token in screenshots, issues, prompts or versioned files. If you receive name_taken, choose another alias or use the token you saved for that identity.

04 / A DECISION THAT LASTS

Save the context.

In the second terminal, create a decision and read it back. The value 0 means this is a new entry. To update it, use the latest version you read; an old version causes a conflict instead of overwriting another change.

Windows · PowerShell
& $cli memory put $projectId architecture --content "One worktree per task" --expected-version 0
& $cli memory list $projectId
& $cli memory put $projectId architecture --content "One worktree and one branch per task" --expected-version 1
& $cli memory list $projectId
macOS and Linux · Bash
"$cli" memory put "$project_id" architecture --content "One worktree per task" --expected-version 0
"$cli" memory list "$project_id"
"$cli" memory put "$project_id" architecture --content "One worktree and one branch per task" --expected-version 1
"$cli" memory list "$project_id"

The final result includes the decision with version: 2. This memory holds shared project text, so save useful decisions and avoid credentials or private information.

05 / COORDINATION WITH EXPIRY

Acquire a file lease.

This example leases the relative name file:src/app.py for 120 seconds, displays the lease and releases it. It does not create or modify that file. Run the whole block before the lease expires.

Windows · PowerShell
$leases = & $cli lease acquire $projectId my-agent file:src/app.py --ttl 120 | ConvertFrom-Json
& $cli lease list $projectId
& $cli lease release $projectId $leases[0].id $leases[0].fence
& $cli events $projectId
macOS and Linux · Bash
lease_json="$("$cli" lease acquire "$project_id" my-agent file:src/app.py --ttl 120)"
lease_id="$(printf '%s' "$lease_json" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["id"])')"
fence="$(printf '%s' "$lease_json" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["fence"])')"
"$cli" lease list "$project_id"
"$cli" lease release "$project_id" "$lease_id" "$fence"
"$cli" events "$project_id"

Releasing the lease returns released: true. Leases are cooperative: the coordinator prevents incompatible acquisitions, but cannot stop an external editor from writing to the file. If the lease expires, acquire a new one and use its new values.

YOU HAVE A STARTING POINT

Continue at your own pace.

Run cshcli provider status to check your providers. Chat requires your own compatible account or API key and may incur costs; the conversational entry point, cshcli, can include a capped index of your current folder and read a text file when you explicitly request /ver <path>. It reads files without executing them. Follow the provider guide to choose the right integration.

To try invitations between identities on this machine, see the invitation workflow. There is no service between machines, execution sandbox or configured deployment provider yet. The project status describes the verified limits.

When you finish, press Ctrl + C in the first terminal to stop the server. In the second, clear the session token with Remove-Item Env:CSHCLI_TOKEN in PowerShell or unset CSHCLI_TOKEN in Bash. Local data remains in SQLite; keep that folder if you want to preserve your projects.
